writeup: TIC 231917790 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 2.248119 days, detected through automated analysis of TESS photometry. The primary eclipse produces a dimming of 18.52 percent, while no secondary eclipse was detected. The signal has a high statistical significance of 511.6 in the automated period-search algorithm, and pixel-level analysis confirms the signal with a peak signal-to-noise ratio of 187.3, though the centroid offset of 3.3 arcseconds from the target warrants attention. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs. However, the eclipse depths show significant alternation between odd and even eclipses, suggesting the true orbital period is double the initially measured value. This unusual pattern remains an open question about the system's nature.
